questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Ephemeral
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Fleeting**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Ephemeral"** means lasting for a very short time; something that is temporary or momentary. (क्षणभंगुर)

 
 
• **Example:** The beauty of a sunset is ephemeral, disappearing as the night approaches.
 
 
 
• **"Fleeting"** is a synonym of ephemeral, meaning something that passes swiftly, is short-lived, or momentary. (क्षणिक)
 
 
• **Example:** Their happiness was fleeting, as reality quickly set in.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can conclude that the most appropriate synonym of **'Ephemeral'** is **'Fleeting'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Fleeting**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Persistent** (दृढ़): Continuing firmly or obstinately in a course of action in spite of difficulty or opposition.

 
 
• **Example:** Her persistent efforts finally paid off, and she achieved her goal.
 
 
 
• **Durable** (टिकाऊ): Able to withstand wear, pressure, or damage; long-lasting.
 
 
• **Example:** The new phone is highly durable and can survive accidental drops.
 
 
 
• **Permanent** (स्थायी): Lasting or intended to last or remain unchanged indefinitely.
 
 
• **Example:** The couple decided to settle in a permanent residence after traveling for years.

questions.question:

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate set of words to fill the blanks.

I was trying to ________ a pen to sign a form as my brother had been ________ Rupees 500 for breaking the traffic rules.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "**find**" is appropriate in the first blank as it refers to searching or locating something, such as a pen.
 
• The word "**fined**" is appropriate in the second blank as it indicates a monetary penalty imposed, such as for breaking traffic rules.
 
• The other options do not fit the context logically or grammatically.

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *I was trying to find__ a pen to sign a form as my brother had been __fined__ Rupees 500 for breaking the traffic rules.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Lend:** means to give something temporarily. (e.g., lend a pen)
 
• **Find:** means to locate or discover something. (e.g., find a pen)
 
• **Fined:** refers to imposing a monetary penalty. (e.g., fined for breaking a rule)

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

This is the __old__ tree in the colony.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. oldest .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence refers to a comparison among all the trees in the colony, implying the oldest one.
 
• The word **"oldest"** is the superlative form of the adjective **"old"**, and it is used to compare more than two items or entities.
 
• Other options such as **"older"** are used for comparative purposes between two entities, and **"most old"** is grammatically incorrect.
 
• The word **"elder"** is typically used to refer to people, not objects like trees, and hence is not appropriate in this context.

Correct sentence: *This is the **oldest** tree in the colony*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Comparative Adjectives:**
 
 
• Used to compare two entities.
 
• **Example:** This tree is **older** than the one in the garden.
 
 
 
• **Superlative Adjectives:**
 
 
• Used to compare more than two entities to identify the one with the highest degree of the quality.
 
• **Example:** This is the **oldest** tree in the colony.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Select the appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word to make the sentence grammatically correct.

This novel is __more interesting__ of all in the library.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. the most interesting .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence is: *This novel is more interesting of all in the library*.
 
• Here, the sentence is comparing one novel with all others in the library, which requires a superlative adjective.
 
• The phrase **“more interesting of all”** is grammatically incorrect because when comparing one item to a group, the superlative form of the adjective must be used.
 
• The correct superlative form of "interesting" is **"the most interesting."**
 
• Thus, the corrected sentence becomes: *This novel is the most interesting of all in the library*.

Correct sentence: *This novel is **the most interesting** of all in the library*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Positive Degree:**
 
 
• Used when no comparison is made.
 
• **Example:** This novel is interesting.
 
 
 
• **Comparative Degree:**
 
 
• Used to compare two items.
 
• **Example:** This novel is more interesting than that one.
 
 
 
• **Superlative Degree:**
 
 
• Used to compare one item with all others in a group.
 
• **Example:** This novel is the most interesting of all.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the idiom from the options given below:

A square peg in a round hole

options.text: a person who is criminal by nature
a person who fits the job
a person who does not fit the job

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. **a person who does not fit the job**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"A square peg in a round hole"** refers to a person who is unsuited for the position or situation they are placed in. (ऐसा व्यक्ति जो किसी कार्य या स्थिति के लिए अनुपयुक्त हो।)

 
 
• **Example:** John is a square peg in a round hole in his current job; he lacks the skills required for this role.
 
 
 
• **Correct Meaning:** A person who does not fit the job. (ऐसा व्यक्ति जो काम के लिए उपयुक्त न हो।)
 
 
• **Example:** Hiring Sarah for this technical role was a mistake; she is a square peg in a round hole here.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: A person who is criminal by nature** (स्वभाव से अपराधी व्यक्ति): Refers to someone with a tendency to commit crimes.

 
 
• **Example:** His repeated offenses show that he is criminal by nature.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: A person who fits the job** (ऐसा व्यक्ति जो काम के लिए उपयुक्त हो): Refers to someone whose skills and abilities are perfectly suited for the role.
 
 
• **Example:** Jane is the perfect candidate for this role; she fits the job like a glove.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: A person who is bankrupt** (दिवालिया व्यक्ति): Refers to someone who is financially insolvent or without money.
 
 
• **Example:** After his business failed, he was declared bankrupt.

questions.question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

The house seemed much __far__ than she expected.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. farther.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"far"** refers to distance, and its comparative form is **"farther."**
 
• **"Farther"** is used for physical distance, while **"further"** is used for figurative or abstract distance.
 
• The given sentence requires the comparative form of "far," as it is comparing the distance to her expectations.
 
• Other options like **"farthest,"** **"farer,"** and **"more far"** are incorrect because:
 
 
• **"Farthest"** is the superlative form and is used when comparing three or more entities.
 
• **"Farer"** is not a valid word in English.
 
• **"More far"** is grammatically incorrect, as "farther" is the standard comparative form.
 
 

Correct sentence: *The house seemed much farther than she expected.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Comparatives:**

 
 
• Comparatives are used to compare two things.
 
• For adjectives with one syllable, add **"-er"** (e.g., "taller").
 
• For longer adjectives, use **"more"** before the adjective (e.g., "more beautiful").
 
 
 
• **Superlatives:**
 
 
• Superlatives are used to describe the highest degree among three or more things.
 
• For adjectives with one syllable, add **"-est"** (e.g., "tallest").
 
• For longer adjectives, use **"most"** before the adjective (e.g., "most beautiful").

questions.question:

The athlete's (languid) performance disappointed the fans as well as coaches.
questions.solution:

• **"Vigorous" **is the antonym of languid. It means full of energy, forceful, strong, and active. (जोशीला, ऊर्जावान)
 
 
• **Example:** The vigorous debate between the candidates showcased their deep knowledge on the subject.
 
 
 
• Hence, the opposite of **"Languid"** is **"Vigorous"**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Vigorous**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Listless **(उदासीन): Lacking energy or enthusiasm, similar to languid.
 
 
• **Example:** She became listless after hearing the disappointing news.
 
 
 
• **Lethargic** (सुस्त): Drowsy, sluggish, or lacking energy.
 
 
• **Example:** The hot weather made everyone feel lethargic and unwilling to move.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'.

While I was teaching the elder one, __the younger one take an opportunity and ran away.__

options.text: the younger one took an opportunity and ran away
the younger one will take an opportunity and ran away
the younger one has taken an opportunity and ran away

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. the younger one took an opportunity and ran away.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the past continuous tense, as indicated by **"While I was teaching"**.
 
• In this context, the action performed by the younger one (taking the opportunity and running away) must also be in the past tense to maintain consistency with the sentence structure.
 
• The correct past tense of "take" is "took," so the appropriate substitution is "the younger one took an opportunity and ran away."

Correct sentence: *While I was teaching the elder one, the younger one **took an opportunity and ran away**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Past Continuous Tense:**
 
 
• **Structure:** Subject + was/were + verb(-ing) + object.
 
• **Usage:** Describes an action that was ongoing at a specific time in the past.
 
• **Example:** I was reading a book when the phone rang.
 
 
 
• **Simple Past Tense:**
 
 
• **Structure:** Subject + past form of the verb + object.
 
• **Usage:** Describes actions that were completed in the past.
 
• **Example:** She took a deep breath and started speaking.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.

Raman is as __worse__ as Raju in solving mathematical problems.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. bad .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence as given contains a grammatical error in the phrase **"as worse as Raju."**
 
• The correct comparative adjective to use with "as...as" is **"bad."**
 
• Since we are making a comparison of equality, the structure to follow is **"as + adjective (positive degree) + as."**

Correct sentence: *Raman is as bad as Raju in solving mathematical problems.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Comparative adjectives:**

 
 
• **Worse:** Used to compare two things when one is of a poorer quality, condition, or standard (e.g., "This situation is worse than before.").
 
• **Bad:** Used in the positive degree when no direct comparison is made (e.g., "This is bad.").
 
• **Worst:** Used in the superlative degree when comparing more than two things (e.g., "This is the worst day of my life.").
